themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Surge
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints spiked to 123 this week, up 129% from the 8-week average of 53.8 weekly complaints—a statistically extreme spike (z-score: 10.86) suggesting a sudden outbreak of sanitation failures affecting Crown Heights residents.
evidence: 123 unsanitary condition complaints filed this week vs. 53.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
129% increase represents statistically extreme deviation (z-score: 10.86, severity: high)
Community board has filed repeated 'Other cleaning requests' to Department of Sanitation—recurring unfunded ask suggests chronic understaffing or service gaps
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Visit highest-complaint blocks; interview residents and building superintendents about what's driving the spike (pest infestations, garbage collection failures, illegal dumping?)
Sanitation department accountability: Request recent service data, staffing levels, and response times; ask whether this spike reflects service cuts or an acute environmental event

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 3 this week from a near-zero 8-week baseline (0.1 weekly average)—a 2300% spike—signaling rapid expansion of street dining, potential street obstruction, or noise/compliance enforcement concerns in the district.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints filed this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
2300% increase (z-score: 8.69, severity: high) indicates sudden emergence of complaint category
Aligns with post-pandemic outdoor dining infrastructure expansion; potential indicator of new dining venues or encroachment onto sidewalks/parking
reporting_angles: Map the complaints: Identify which blocks or restaurants are generating complaints; assess whether outdoor dining is blocking sidewalks, creating noise, or violating permit terms
Follow-up on 1034-1042 Atlantic Ave FRESH Pt. 2 development: Does this retail/dining project explain the spike, or is it independent expansion?

themes_detail.label: Flooring & Safety Hazards Rise
themes_detail.summary: Flooring/stairs complaints surged to 31 this week, up 114% from 14.5 weekly average, and safety complaints doubled (15 vs. 7.5 average)—suggesting accelerating building code violations or deferred maintenance affecting resident safety this week.
evidence: 31 flooring/stairs complaints this week vs. 14.5 weekly average (114% increase, z-score: 4.12)
15 safety complaints this week vs. 7.5 weekly average (100% increase, z-score: 4.01)
495 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (300 alterations + 71 alteration COs) suggest active construction; complaints may reflect incomplete work or violations
reporting_angles: Connect to construction: Cross-reference DOB permits with complaint addresses; identify which properties are under alteration and whether violations stem from active work or post-project neglect
Landlord accountability: Investigate repeat violators—buildings with multiple flooring/safety complaints; seek DOB enforcement records and open violations

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Matters Up 260%
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints jumped to 9 this week from a 2.5 weekly average—a 260% spike—potentially signaling rising street-level quality-of-life concerns (disorderly conduct, trespassing, loitering) in the district.
evidence: 9 non-emergency police complaints this week vs. 2.5 weekly average (260% increase, z-score: 4.33)
311 data does not break down complaint subtypes; underlying issues (encampments, open-air drug activity, group congregation) unclear
Community board budget requests include 'homeless facilities' expansion, suggesting awareness of street-level social service gaps
reporting_angles: Request NYPD precinct data: Ask 73rd Precinct for detail on what types of non-emergency calls spike aligned with this week's 311 surge
Homelessness angle: Investigate whether spike correlates with increased encampments, displacement, or weather-driven street concentration

themes_detail.label: Electrical & Construction Hazards (Lagging)
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 3 two weeks ago (up 1100% from 0.2 baseline), and general construction/plumbing complaints reached 39 two weeks ago (up 236%)—sustained building-work pattern that may indicate ongoing hazardous renovation activity or infrastructure failures.
evidence: 3 electrical complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
39 general construction/plumbing complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 11.6 weekly average (236% increase, z-score: 5.25)
102 new building permits and 300 alterations filed in last 90 days; spike 2 weeks ago may reflect cumulative effect of active job sites
reporting_angles: DOB inspection follow-up: Request violation records for properties with active permits filed 8–12 weeks ago (now mid-construction); assess whether electrical/plumbing violations are being cited
Contractor accountability: Identify repeat contractors across multiple permits; assess whether pattern suggests systemic code compliance issues
